newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FAI Insurances to cut home loan rate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FAI Insurances to cut home loan rate.

text.p: FAI Insurances Ltd said on Friday its home loans division had cut the rate on its RMT standard vairable home loan by 0.5 percentage points to 7.95 percent, effective immediately for new borrowers and from December 25 for existing borrowers.
"FAI's interest rate cut pre-empts an anticipated cut in official interest rates by the Reserve Bank," the company's chief executive, Rodney Adler told a press briefing.
Adler said FAI was now offering the lowest standard variable interest rate in Australia.

Asked how much further he saw Australian interest rates falling, Adler said: "We have a lot of scope as a nation to reduce interest rates more. I certainly see another 50 basis points, in fact I can see a whole percent, after that it depends on the economy."
Adler and the managing director of FAI's home loan division, John McGee, both said there was an active home loan price war occuring in Australia's financial services industry.
"I think we have lived in a home loan rate war, banks building societies, mortgage orginators and all for the last two years and the borrowing public has been the big winners from this," McGee said.
McGee said FAI's home loan rate was last under the eight percent level in September 1994.
Earlier today, Australia's largest mortagage originator, Aussie Home Loans said it would cut its variable mortgage rate by 0.66 percentage points to 7.99 percent.
